nodes.description: Cerebellar atrophy, often with vermian involvement, that appears to develop after birth: a patient with a normal cerebellum at 15 months had atrophy at 33 months, and another had atrophy on follow-up imaging at age 2 years that was not reported initially. Its absence on an early scan therefore does not exclude the diagnosis. In the oldest patient the atrophy was stable between ages 21 and 29.

nodes.description: Biallelic GPAA1 variants. The founding cohort carried two frameshift alleles, one intronic splice-region allele that lowered GPAA1 mRNA, and six missense alleles; the pooled 2026 review counts 28 variants, mostly missense, with frameshift, splicing and one nonsense allele. No patient has two null alleles, so the disease state is read as partial rather than complete loss of GPAA1 function. GPAA1 is a non-catalytic subunit, so the activity it loses is that of the whole transamidase complex.

nodes.description: The GPI transamidase complex in the endoplasmic reticulum cleaves the C-terminal GPI attachment signal of precursor proteins and transfers the GPI anchor to the new C terminus. PIGK carries the catalytic residues; structural work indicates GPAA1 is not itself catalytic but is required for the complex to work.

nodes.description: GPI-anchored proteins in the nervous system take part in axon growth, regeneration, synapse formation and synaptic plasticity. Their reduction is the proposed route to the developmental delay, hypotonia and epilepsy, but no study has attributed these features to a particular GPI-anchored protein in GPAA1 deficiency.

nodes.description: Hypothesized mechanism for osteopenia: reduced surface alkaline phosphatase on osteoblasts lowers bone formation. This is the authors' hypothesis, not a measured result, and epilepsy, antiseizure drugs and reduced mobility independently lower bone density in these patients.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum of GPI Anchoring Deficiency Due to Biallelic Variants in GPAA1.
evidence.snippet: Osteopenia and osteoporosis are hypothesized to be secondary to decreased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) expression on the surface of osteoblasts, impairing their function and leading to decreased bone formation and therefore bone mineral density.

nodes.description: Precursor proteins that are not anchored do not reach the cell surface as GPI-anchored proteins, so the surface density of the whole class falls. Patient leukocytes showed reduced FLAER (total GPI-anchored proteins), CD16 and CD59; patient fibroblasts showed reduced CD73 and CD109. Lentiviral re-expression of wild-type GPAA1 partly rescued the fibroblast deficit. With over 150 GPI-anchored proteins, no single one has been shown to account for any clinical feature.
